core_obligations: Apply the associated primes criterion to get injectivity (proof lines 5466-5467).
Replace the target by a finitely generated submodule containing the image and note the hypotheses persist (proof lines 5468-5475).
Assume the target is finite, form the cokernel, and translate the two cases of the hypothesis into statements about its depth (proof lines 5476-5485).
Conclude that the cokernel has no associated primes and therefore is zero (proof lines 5485-5487).
proof_roadmap: Injectivity from the associated primes criterion (proof lines 5466-5467).
Reduce to a finite target (proof lines 5468-5475).
Kill the cokernel through depth and associated primes (proof lines 5476-5487).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a local criterion for a map from a finite module to be an isomorphism: at every prime either the map is already an isomorphism or the source has depth at least two and the prime is not associated to the target. The proof first obtains injectivity from the companion associated primes criterion, then reduces to the case where the target is finite by replacing it with a finitely generated submodule containing the image, and finally forms the cokernel: the hypotheses translate into the cokernel being either zero or of depth at least one at every prime, which by the behaviour of depth in short exact sequences means the cokernel has no associated primes at all, hence vanishes.
